title: Telemetry Normalizer: canonical spans and histograms for deterministic SLO rollups
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Our current SLO rollups and burn-rate alerts are noisy and non-deterministic because span naming, metric timer buckets, and per-route tag cardinality vary across services and language SDKs. This makes cross-service latencies hard to attribute and causes frequent false-positive paging. Goals: 1) Introduce a lightweight Telemetry Normalizer microservice that canonicalizes span names and HTTP route tags at ingestion; 2) Convert timer metrics into compact HDR histograms / t-digest summaries for deterministic SLO evaluation; 3) Emit a unified low-cardinality signal stream for the SLO engine and anomaly scorer; 4) Provide a migration mapping UI and audit logs so teams can validate transformations before lock-in.

Success criteria: a) End-to-end SLO evaluation latency for a 1M QPS trace/metric stream < 3s additional overhead; b) 40-60% reduction in unique metric series used for SLO rollups across top 50 services; c) 30% reduction in noisy burn-rate pages in first month after rollout; d) Backwards-compatible raw telemetry retention unchanged.

Design overview: - Ingest: OTLP traces/metrics forwarded to a Kafka topic or directly via a small HTTP adapter. - Normalizer: rule engine with ordered transforms: canonical_span (regex + route templating), tag_flatten (remove high-cardinality keys), histogramize (aggregate timer samples into HDR bins), sampling_affinity (consistent sampling for heavy routes). Rules are editable via Confluence + YAML stored in ConfigStore and can be hot-reloaded. - Output: two sinks: (1) canonical telemetry stream to SLO engine / metrics TSDB; (2) raw telemetry passthrough to cold storage for audits. - Observability: internal health metrics, per-service normalization delta dashboard, and a validation UI showing before/after examples.

Tradeoffs & constraints: - Some precision lost when collapsing spans/tags; mitigated by raw passthrough and feature-flagged rollout by team. - CPU/Memory cost for on-the-fly histogramization; we'll use native C++ HDR library with JNI wrappers for high-throughput paths. - Need clear ownership and mapping rules to avoid semantic drift.

Rollout plan: 1) Build prototype for 5 high-traffic services under a feature flag; 2) Run side-by-side for 2 weeks and measure SLO delta; 3) Provide mapping review with service owners; 4) Gradually enable for additional teams with A/B traffic splits; 5) Full activation and deprecation of old rollups after 90 days.

Telemetry & QA: dashboards (Grafana) for normalization rate, rule-miss rate, additional latency P50/P99 for telemetry pipeline, and a 'diff' view between canonical and raw SLOs. Automated tests: unit rule engine tests, fuzz tests for regex rules, integration test that validates histograms against synthetic timers, and end-to-end load test in staging (target 2x current peak).

Links: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Telemetry+Normalizer; Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/4128; Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/obs-normalizer/normalizer-overview
